title: Externalized State-Machine Routing (BPEL Emulation)
pattern: Moving core application control flow and state transitions out of the language's native structures into an uncompiled external configuration file (like a CSV or text file).
why_bad: It divorces the application's control flow from compile-time verification, breaks calling graph analysis, and makes debugging almost impossible. A simple typo in a state configuration file causes a runtime crash or silent logic bypass.
detection: A parser at startup that ingests transition mappings, state transitions, or workflow steps from text files (YAML, JSON, CSV) to orchestrate core function calls.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Complex distributed business orchestrations (like long-running sagas with human-in-the-loop steps) may require externalized metadata for durability.
source: [Robert C. Martin Series] Robert C. Martin - _Clean Architecture_ A Craftsman’s Guide to Software Structure and Design_ (2017, Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 34 "Craft Dispatch System".
